title: Trump Weighs Ousting Joint Chiefs Chair or CENTCOM Chief as Hegseth Faces Impeachment Push
dek: The White House denies reports that Hegseth or Rubio will leave, while the Washington Post reports Trump is considering removing two senior military leaders.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Pentagon, headquarters of the US Department of Defense (file photo)
image.credit: DoD photo by Master Sgt. Ken Hammond, US Air Force / Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: The Washington Post reported on Thursday that Trump might be considering ousting Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, or Adm. Brad Cooper, the Centcom chief, BBC reported.
The White House and State Department called reports that Hegseth and Rubio might leave "fake news," BBC reported.
Trump told ABC News he had received "calls about" Hegseth but had "every intention" of keeping him.
Rep. Thomas Massie said he will trigger an impeachment resolution against Hegseth early next week, according to Politico as reported by BBC.
body:
President Donald Trump is weighing whether to remove two senior military leaders, the Washington Post reported on Thursday, as Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces a push for impeachment after Republican losses in the midterm elections.

## Military leaders under consideration

The Post reported that Trump might oust Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, or Adm. Brad Cooper, the head of US Central Command. Both played significant roles advising on the Iran war, which began eight months ago, BBC reported. The reporting reviewed for this story does not say whether a decision has been made.

## White House denials

The White House denied reports that Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio might leave their jobs in a post-election shakeup. The State Department also called the reports "fake news." Rubio told The New York Times that working for Trump until the end of his term "has always been my plan."

Trump told ABC News he had received "calls about" Hegseth but had "every intention" of keeping him. Later on Thursday he told reporters that "Pete Hegseth has done a fantastic job." Hegseth posted a video statement defending his record: "They attack us because we are effective... We will not back down."

## Impeachment push

Republican Rep. Thomas Massie, who is leaving Congress, said he will push ahead with a resolution to impeach Hegseth. He told Politico he will trigger it early next week, when Congress returns, BBC reported. Earlier reporting by NBC News said the House had punted the vote until after Election Day.

## Context

Trump and Vice President JD Vance have both blamed the Iran war for Republican losses that gave Democrats control of the House and Senate, BBC reported. Vance has written on X that "The reason we lost is the war."

## What we do not know

No official has confirmed a removal decision on Caine or Cooper. Reporting reviewed for this story does not say how many House Republicans would back the impeachment resolution.

sources.title: White House denies Hegseth and Rubio to leave jobs after Republican election losses
Republicans quickly turn against Pete Hegseth after midterms rout
House could vote next week to impeach Hegseth as GOP support wavers
